elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party (carve-out now limited to Client)

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: A change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement.

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: carve-out is limited to "an assignment by Client"; Vendor retains no successor right
no notice mechanic appears in the revised clause

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are present: Customer affiliate and successor carve-outs, Vendor consent requirement, reasonableness standard on Customer's consent, competitor bar, and no change-of-control termination right for Vendor.
Deletion of "financially responsible" is required because the preferred affiliate right must be unqualified; the edit otherwise leaves the mutual consent baseline sentence intact.
The inserted sentences are short and each maps to a distinct missing preferred element (reasonableness, competitor bar, change-of-control), so no unnecessary boilerplate or whole-clause rewrite.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic), but the locked target level is preferred and that bargain is complete.
No undefined terms introduced; Client and TrueLink are defined parties and no dangling mechanic results.
